meanings.note: C'est un signe = it's a sign. Masculine noun ('le signe', plural 'les signes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sign'.

examples.text: C'est le signe de la percée.
examples.trans: It is the sign of the breakthrough.

examples.text: C'est donc un très bon signe?
examples.trans: Is that a very good sign?

meanings.note: Passé composé with 'être'. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to go out; to leave'.

meanings.en: sortir avec quelqu'un = to go out with, to date someone
meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to go out; to leave'.

examples.text: Sortir avec l'assistante de son agent.
examples.trans: To go out with his agent's assistant.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas très intelligent de sortir avec l'assistante de son agent.
examples.trans: It's not very smart to go out with his agent's assistant.

meanings.en: se souvenir de = to remember, to recall
meanings.note: Conjugated like venir. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to remember (se souvenir)'.

examples.text: Je ne me souviens pas, Gabriel.
Bonjour, je me souviens très bien de vous.
examples.trans: Hello, I remember you very well.

meanings.note: casual object pronoun, before the verb

examples.text: Je voulais te faire la surprise.
Je ne sais pas. Je voulais te faire la surprise.
examples.trans: I don't know. I wanted to surprise you.

meanings.note: takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: one person you know well: friends, family, close colleagues

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi? Mardi, tu as le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday? On Tuesday you've got the Kechiche film.

meanings.note: ne fais pas cette tête = don't look like that; faire la tête = to sulk

meanings.en: c'est dans ma tête = it's all in my head
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la tête', plural 'les têtes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'head'.

examples.trans: Maybe it's all in my head.

meanings.note: indefinite article; des in the plural
Number; l'un = one of them. Spoken French det expression meaning 'a', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to sell'.

examples.text: Je ne veux pas travailler à l'agence. Je veux vendre.
examples.trans: I don't want to work at the agency. I want to sell.

meanings.note: En voiture = by car. Feminine noun ('la voiture', plural 'les voitures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'car'.

examples.text: Je n'ai pas de voiture, je suis à pied!
examples.trans: I don't have a car, I'm on foot!

examples.text: Arrête la voiture! Gabriel, arrête la voiture!
examples.trans: Stop the car! Gabriel, stop the car!

meanings.note: + noun or infinitive. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to want'.
Imparfait, softer. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to want'.

examples.trans: I just want to see Mathias.

examples.text: Je voulais te faire la surprise.
Je ne suis pas actrice. Je veux juste voir Mathias.
examples.trans: I'm not an actress. I just want to see Mathias.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'true'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Descriptive French adjective meaning 'true'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: La terre, elle est vraie. Elle ne sait pas mentir.
examples.trans: The earth is honest. It doesn't know how to lie.

meanings.note: Dire la vérité = to tell the truth. Feminine abstract noun formed with '-ité' (from Latin '-itas', English '-ity'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'truth'.

examples.text: Tu n'as jamais dit la vérité sur nous!
examples.trans: You never told the truth about us!

meanings.note: Il y a = there is / there are. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'there'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
J'y pense = I think about it. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'there'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: S'il vous plaît. Il n'y a rien entre Mathias et moi, d'accord?
examples.trans: Please. There's nothing between Mathias and me, okay?

meanings.note: Place: à Paris, à mon cours. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Time: à midi. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.en: au = à + le, aux = à + les
meanings.note: Contractions. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
masculine, even though it ends in -e

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.
examples.trans: Tarantino won't take Cécile. A problem with her age.

meanings.note: Informal for cela. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'that'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
With time. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'that'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
épouser quelqu'un = to marry someone

examples.trans: He is going to marry her.

meanings.note: The most common verb. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be'.
Ce + est. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be'.
